title: Audit Procedures for Fixed Assets (Property, Plant & Equipment)
exam_relevance: MODERATELY TESTED - Expect 2-4 questions on CPA AUD exam about testing additions/disposals, depreciation testing, physical inspection, impairment, and capitalization vs. expense decisions. Also heavily tested on FAR for accounting treatment.
learning_objectives: Understand procedures for testing fixed asset additions
Know procedures for testing fixed asset disposals and retirements
Understand depreciation testing and recalculation procedures
Know when and how to perform physical inspection of fixed assets
Understand procedures for testing impairment of long-lived assets
Know how to evaluate capitalization vs. expense decisions
Understand lease classification testing (operating vs finance leases)
Know assertions related to fixed assets and appropriate procedures for each

introduction.why_important: Fixed assets (property, plant, and equipment) are typically material long-lived assets. Key risks include: (1) improper capitalization of expenses or expensing of assets, (2) incorrect depreciation calculations, (3) failure to recognize impairment, (4) unrecorded disposals, and (5) lease misclassification.

key_standards.auditing: AU-C Section 330 (Performing Audit Procedures in Response to Assessed Risks)

introduction.exam_importance: Focus on: testing additions (vouch to invoices), depreciation recalculation, physical inspection, and capitalization vs. expense. Lease classification is also tested (though more heavily on FAR).

assertions_for_fixed_assets.description: Understanding which assertions are at risk helps determine appropriate procedures

existence_occurrence.risk: Recording assets that don't exist or that were disposed of but not removed from books (overstatement)
existence_occurrence.primary_procedure: PHYSICAL INSPECTION - physically observe and inspect significant assets
other_procedures: Vouch additions to supporting documentation (invoices, contracts)
Test disposals to ensure properly removed from books
Trace sample from fixed asset register to physical assets
existence_occurrence.exam_emphasis: Physical inspection addresses EXISTENCE for significant assets

completeness.risk: Failing to record asset acquisitions or capitalizing items that should be capitalized (understatement)
procedures: Test for unrecorded additions (examine repair/maintenance expense for capitalized items)
Review lease agreements to identify finance leases requiring capitalization
Trace physical assets to fixed asset register (ensure all are recorded)
Analytical procedures (compare to prior year, budget)

rights_and_obligations.risk: Recording assets not owned (e.g., operating leases) or failing to record assets owned (finance leases)
procedures: Review lease agreements to verify proper classification (operating vs finance)
Examine titles and ownership documents for major assets (real estate, vehicles)
Review purchase agreements and payment records
Identify assets pledged as collateral (affects presentation disclosure)
rights_and_obligations.exam_note: Finance lease = capitalize (ownership transfers). Operating lease = expense (no ownership).

valuation_accuracy.risk: Assets recorded at incorrect cost, depreciation miscalculated, or impairment not recognized
procedures: Vouch acquisition cost to invoices and supporting documents
Recalculate depreciation expense and accumulated depreciation
Test useful lives and salvage values for reasonableness
Evaluate indicators of impairment and test impairment if necessary
Verify proper capitalization of interest on self-constructed assets
valuation_accuracy.exam_emphasis: Depreciation recalculation and impairment testing are key valuation procedures

presentation_and_disclosure.risk: Improper classification, inadequate disclosure of depreciation methods, pledged assets, or commitments
procedures: Review classification (land, buildings, equipment, construction in progress)
Verify depreciation methods and useful lives disclosed
Identify and disclose pledged assets
Review commitments for future asset purchases

testing_fixed_asset_additions.description: Verify additions to fixed assets are properly recorded at correct cost and should be capitalized

obtain_schedule_of_additions.procedure: Obtain client-prepared schedule of all fixed asset additions for the year
obtain_schedule_of_additions.contents: Description, date acquired, cost, depreciation method, useful life
obtain_schedule_of_additions.reconcile: Reconcile total additions to general ledger fixed asset accounts

vouch_additions_to_supporting_documents.procedure: Select sample of additions and vouch to supporting documentation

vouch_to.vendor_invoices: Verify cost per invoice matches recorded amount (tests valuation)
vouch_to.contracts: For major purchases, review purchase contracts

verify: Recorded cost is correct per invoice (including sales tax, freight, installation if capitalizable)
Asset was actually acquired during the year
Asset exists and is in use or available for use
inspect_major_additions.timing: Can inspect at interim or year-end

evaluate_capitalization_decision.procedure: Evaluate whether additions should be CAPITALIZED or EXPENSED

capitalization_criteria.provides_future_benefit: Asset must provide future economic benefit beyond current period
capitalization_criteria.extends_useful_life: For improvements: extends useful life, increases capacity, or improves efficiency
capitalization_criteria.not_ordinary_repairs: Ordinary repairs and maintenance should be expensed, not capitalized

examples_capitalize: Major renovations that extend useful life
evaluate_capitalization_decision.red_flag: Capitalizing routine repairs/maintenance inflates assets and income (fraud concern)
evaluate_capitalization_decision.exam_emphasis: Know difference between capital expenditure (capitalize) and revenue expenditure (expense)

verify_capitalized_costs_appropriate.procedure: Verify all costs included in asset cost are appropriate to capitalize
capitalize_these_costs: Testing costs to get asset ready for use
do_not_capitalize: Costs after asset is ready for use
Administrative and overhead costs (unless directly attributable)

test_for_unrecorded_additions.procedure: Test for additions that should have been capitalized but were expensed
test_for_unrecorded_additions.scan_expense_accounts: Scan REPAIRS AND MAINTENANCE expense, RENT expense for large or unusual items that may be capital in nature
red_flags: Large repairs expense amounts (may be betterments requiring capitalization)
Payments described as 'improvements' or 'renovations' in expense accounts
Operating lease payments that should be finance leases

testing_fixed_asset_disposals_and_retire.description: Verify assets disposed of or retired are properly removed from books and gain/loss calculated correctly

obtain_schedule_of_disposals.procedure: Obtain schedule of all asset disposals, retirements, sales during year
obtain_schedule_of_disposals.contents: Asset description, original cost, accumulated depreciation, sale proceeds, gain/loss

vouch_disposals_to_supporting_documents.procedure: Select sample of disposals and vouch to supporting documentation
examine: Sales invoices or contracts (for assets sold)
Board minutes approving sale of major assets
verify: Asset was removed from fixed asset register

recalculate_gain_or_loss.procedure: Recalculate gain or loss on disposal
recalculate_gain_or_loss.formula: Proceeds - Net Book Value = Gain or Loss
recalculate_gain_or_loss.net_book_value: Original Cost - Accumulated Depreciation at disposal date
verify: Depreciation updated through disposal date (partial year if mid-year disposal)
recalculate_gain_or_loss.exam_note: Disposal gain/loss = Proceeds minus NBV. Must depreciate through disposal date first.

verify_asset_removed_from_books.procedure: Verify both original cost and accumulated depreciation removed from books
journal_entry_should_show: DR: Accumulated Depreciation (amount accumulated at disposal)
DR or CR: Gain or Loss on Disposal (balancing amount)
verify_asset_removed_from_books.common_error: Failing to remove accumulated depreciation (overstates accumulated depreciation)

test_for_unrecorded_disposals.procedure: Test for assets that were disposed but not removed from books
test_for_unrecorded_disposals.scan_for_old_assets: Review fixed asset register for very old or fully depreciated assets that may no longer exist
test_for_unrecorded_disposals.physical_inspection: During physical inspection, trace items from register to floor - items not found may have been disposed
test_for_unrecorded_disposals.inquiry: Inquire with management about retired or scrapped assets
test_for_unrecorded_disposals.red_flag: Fully depreciated assets still on books may have been discarded but not removed (overstated assets)

depreciation_testing.description: Verify depreciation expense and accumulated depreciation are properly calculated

understanding_depreciation.purpose: Systematic allocation of asset's depreciable cost over its useful life

methods.declining_balance: Accelerated - Rate × Book Value (don't subtract salvage for DB)
methods.units_of_production: Based on usage - (Cost - Salvage) ÷ Total Units × Units This Period

obtain_depreciation_schedule.procedure: Obtain client-prepared depreciation schedule showing all assets
obtain_depreciation_schedule.contents: Asset, cost, accumulated depreciation beginning, depreciation expense, accumulated depreciation ending
obtain_depreciation_schedule.reconcile: Reconcile totals to general ledger (fixed assets, accumulated depreciation, depreciation expense)

recalculate_depreciation.procedure: RECALCULATE depreciation expense for sample of assets
verify: Correct depreciation method used (per company policy)
Partial year depreciation for mid-year additions/disposals
recalculate_depreciation.for_additions: Verify partial year depreciation calculated (e.g., if acquired June 30, only 6 months depreciation in year 1)
recalculate_depreciation.for_disposals: Verify depreciation calculated through disposal date

test_useful_lives_for_reasonableness.procedure: Evaluate whether useful lives are reasonable
compare_to: IRS guidelines (not determinative for GAAP, but useful reference)
Prior years (should be consistent unless change justified)
test_useful_lives_for_reasonableness.too_long_useful_life: Understates depreciation expense and overstates income (fraud concern)

test_salvage_values.procedure: Evaluate whether salvage values are reasonable
test_salvage_values.common: Many companies use zero salvage value for simplicity
test_salvage_values.if_salvage_used: Verify reasonable based on expected residual value at end of useful life

verify_depreciation_method_consistency.procedure: Verify depreciation methods are applied consistently from prior year
verify_depreciation_method_consistency.changes_require_disclosure: Changes in depreciation method or useful life are accounting changes requiring disclosure
verify_depreciation_method_consistency.unjustified_changes: Changes without justification may indicate earnings management

test_fully_depreciated_assets.procedure: Review fully depreciated assets still in use
test_fully_depreciated_assets.verify: No additional depreciation recorded once fully depreciated
test_fully_depreciated_assets.consider: If many assets fully depreciated but still in use, useful lives may have been too short (but don't revise retroactively)

depreciation_expense_to_fixed_assets.interpretation: Should be relatively stable. Large changes may indicate errors, changes in useful lives, or significant additions/disposals.

accumulated_depreciation_to_cost.interpretation: Indicates average age of assets. Higher ratio = older assets. Very high ratio (near 100%) suggests assets fully depreciated.

physical_inspection_of_fixed_assets.description: Physical inspection provides evidence for existence of fixed assets

when_to_perform_inspection.not_always_required: Physical inspection is NOT required for all fixed assets (unlike inventory observation)
perform_when: Significant or major asset additions (new building, major equipment)
Existence is questioned (fraud risk, weak controls)
Assets are portable or easily stolen (computers, tools, vehicles)
when_to_perform_inspection.may_omit_for: Routine assets, immaterial amounts, strong controls, low risk

inspection_procedures.select_sample: Select sample of assets from fixed asset register (typically major or high-value items)

physically_inspect.procedure: Physically locate and inspect the assets
observe: Asset exists and is in the possession of the client
Asset condition is appropriate (operational, not damaged or obsolete)
Asset identification (serial number, asset tag) matches records
physically_inspect.document: Document inspection in working papers (description, location, asset tag number, date inspected)

test_in_both_directions.register_to_floor: Select from fixed asset REGISTER and trace to physical asset (tests EXISTENCE)
test_in_both_directions.floor_to_register: Select assets from FLOOR and trace to fixed asset register (tests COMPLETENESS)

limitations.not_test_valuation: Inspection doesn't test valuation (cost, depreciation) - only existence and condition
limitations.not_test_ownership: Inspection shows possession but doesn't prove ownership (examine titles for that)

impairment_testing.description: Long-lived assets must be tested for impairment when indicators present

when_impairment_testing_required.not_routine: Impairment testing is NOT performed annually (unlike goodwill) - only when INDICATORS present
indicators_of_impairment: Adverse change in business climate or legal factors
Asset idle or plans to dispose before end of useful life
Projected cash flows negative or significantly less than expected
Costs to acquire/construct exceed original expectations
when_impairment_testing_required.exam_note: Impairment test required when INDICATORS present (not annually)

step_1_recoverability_test.question: Is asset recoverable?
step_1_recoverability_test.test: Compare UNDISCOUNTED future cash flows to CARRYING AMOUNT
step_1_recoverability_test.if_undiscounted_cf_less_than_carrying: Asset NOT recoverable - proceed to Step 2 to measure impairment loss
step_1_recoverability_test.exam_critical: Use UNDISCOUNTED cash flows for recoverability test (Step 1)

step_2_measurement.question: How much is the impairment loss?
step_2_measurement.calculation: Carrying Amount - Fair Value = Impairment Loss
step_2_measurement.fair_value: For measurement, use FAIR VALUE (may use DISCOUNTED cash flows or market value)
step_2_measurement.write_down_to_fair_value: Write asset down to fair value, recognize impairment loss
step_2_measurement.exam_critical: Use FAIR VALUE (may be discounted CF) for measurement (Step 2)

impairment_testing_process_per_asc_360.cannot_reverse: Once impairment loss recognized, CANNOT reverse in future periods (even if value recovers)

identify_indicators.procedure: Identify whether impairment indicators are present
identify_indicators.inquire_with_management: Ask about declining asset values, damaged assets, idle assets, disposal plans
identify_indicators.observe_during_inspection: Note damaged or idle assets during physical inspection
identify_indicators.review_cash_flow_projections: Review for negative or declining cash flows from asset use

test_cash_flow_projections.procedure: Evaluate reasonableness of cash flow projections used in recoverability test
assess: Assumptions (growth rates, pricing, volumes) are reasonable
Projections are consistent with business plans and historical experience
Time period is appropriate (remaining useful life)
test_cash_flow_projections.skepticism: Apply professional skepticism - management may be overly optimistic to avoid impairment

if_indicators_present.verify_fair_value_determination: If impairment loss measured, verify fair value determination (appraisal, market comparables, discounted cash flows)
if_indicators_present.recalculate_impairment_loss: Recalculate: Carrying Amount - Fair Value = Impairment Loss

evaluate_if_impairment_should_be_recogni.management_failed_to_recognize: If indicators present but management didn't recognize impairment, discuss and obtain justification
evaluate_if_impairment_should_be_recogni.may_propose_adjustment: If impairment loss should be recognized but wasn't, propose adjusting journal entry

impairment_testing.exam_tip: Step 1: UNDISCOUNTED cash flows vs carrying amount (recoverability). Step 2: Carrying amount - FAIR VALUE = impairment loss (measurement).

capitalization_vs_expense_decisions.description: Critical judgment: should expenditure be capitalized (asset) or expensed (income statement)?

capitalization_criteria.provides_future_benefit: Expenditure must provide future economic benefits beyond current period

for_improvements_to_existing_assets.capitalize_if: Expenditure extends useful life, increases capacity, improves efficiency, or adapts asset to new use
for_improvements_to_existing_assets.expense_if: Ordinary repairs and maintenance that maintain current condition

capitalize_these.betterments: Improvements that extend life or increase capacity (major renovations, upgrades)
capitalize_these.additions: Adding to existing asset (new wing to building)
capitalize_these.replacements_of_major_components: Replacing major component (new roof, new engine)
capitalize_these.interest_during_construction: Capitalized interest on self-constructed assets (construction period only)

expense_these.repairs_and_maintenance: Ordinary repairs that maintain asset in operating condition (painting, oil changes, minor fixes)
expense_these.after_ready_for_use: Costs incurred after asset is ready for use (training, initial operations)
expense_these.unsuccessful_efforts: Costs of unsuccessful development or exploration

audit_procedures.review_capitalization_policy: Understand client's capitalization policy and threshold

test_additions_for_proper_classification.procedure: Examine additions to PP&E and evaluate whether properly capitalized
test_additions_for_proper_classification.vouch_to_invoices: Review invoice descriptions - do they indicate capital improvement or repair?
red_flags: Routine maintenance costs capitalized (overstates assets and income)
Training or initial operation costs capitalized

scan_expense_accounts.procedure: Scan repairs/maintenance expense for large items that should be capitalized
scan_expense_accounts.look_for: Renovations, betterments, additions incorrectly expensed (understates assets)
scan_expense_accounts.exam_scenario: Large payment in repairs expense described as 'building renovation' - should be capitalized

fraud_risk.overstate_income: Capitalize ordinary repairs (increases assets, reduces expenses, overstates income) - common fraud
fraud_risk.understate_income: Expense capital items (reduces assets, increases expenses, understates income) - less common but possible for tax avoidance

lease_classification_testing.description: Verify leases are properly classified as finance leases (capitalized) or operating leases (expensed)

lease_classification_per_asc_842.lessee_perspective: Lessee classifies as finance lease or operating lease
finance_lease_criteria_any_one_triggers_: 1. Transfer of ownership at end of lease
2. Purchase option that lessee is reasonably certain to exercise (bargain purchase option)
3. Lease term is major part of asset's economic life (≥75% threshold eliminated, but still consider)
4. PV of lease payments ≥ substantially all of fair value (≥90% threshold eliminated, but still consider)
5. Asset so specialized that no alternative use to lessor at end of lease
lease_classification_per_asc_842.if_any_criteria_met: FINANCE LEASE - capitalize (record right-of-use asset and lease liability)
lease_classification_per_asc_842.if_no_criteria_met: OPERATING LEASE - expense (but under ASC 842, still recognize ROU asset and liability)
lease_classification_per_asc_842.exam_note_old_rules: CPA exam may still test old criteria (≥75% life, ≥90% PV) - know both old and new ASC 842

audit_procedures_for_leases.obtain_lease_agreements: Obtain all lease agreements for review

review_classification.procedure: Review each lease and verify proper classification
review_classification.evaluate_criteria: Assess whether any of the five finance lease criteria are met
review_classification.verify_calculation: If PV test used, verify PV calculation (rate, payments, term)
review_classification.misclassification_risk: Operating lease should be finance (understates assets and liabilities) or vice versa

verify_lease_liability_and_asset.procedure: For finance leases, verify lease liability and ROU asset properly recorded
verify_lease_liability_and_asset.lease_liability: PV of lease payments at lease commencement
verify_lease_liability_and_asset.rou_asset: Generally equals lease liability (adjusted for prepayments, initial direct costs, lease incentives)

test_lease_payments.procedure: Vouch lease payments to cash disbursements
test_lease_payments.verify: Lease payments made agree to lease agreement terms

scan_rent_expense.procedure: Scan rent/lease expense for large operating leases that may be finance leases
scan_rent_expense.red_flag: Large lease payments that appear to be for asset purchase rather than rental

test_construction_in_progress.description: Construction in progress (CIP) is assets under construction not yet placed in service
procedures: Vouch costs in CIP to invoices, contracts, labor records
Verify only appropriate costs capitalized (materials, labor, capitalized interest)
Verify assets transferred to PP&E when placed in service (begin depreciating)
Inspect construction projects if material
Review for impairment if project delayed, over budget, or questionable viability
test_construction_in_progress.depreciation: CIP is NOT depreciated (not yet in service). Depreciation begins when asset placed in service.

test_capitalized_interest.when_required: Interest capitalized on self-constructed assets or assets requiring time to prepare for use
test_capitalized_interest.period: Capitalize interest during construction period (from start until ready for use)
test_capitalized_interest.stop_when_ready: Stop capitalizing when asset substantially complete and ready for use
test_capitalized_interest.amount: Interest on debt incurred for construction (weighted average accumulated expenditures × interest rate)
audit_procedures: Verify capitalized interest calculation (average expenditures, rate, period)
Verify interest capitalization stopped when asset ready for use
Verify interest not capitalized on assets not qualifying

verify_pledged_assets.procedure: Identify assets pledged as collateral for loans
verify_pledged_assets.review: Loan agreements, security agreements, UCC filings
verify_pledged_assets.confirm: Bank confirmation will indicate pledged assets
verify_pledged_assets.disclosure: Pledged assets must be disclosed in notes to financial statements

fixed_assets_turnover.interpretation: How efficiently company uses fixed assets to generate revenue. Low ratio may indicate excess capacity or idle assets.

repairs_expense_ratio.interpretation: Should be relatively stable. Significant decrease may indicate: (1) capitalizing repairs (fraud), or (2) deferring needed maintenance.

depreciation_to_cost_ratio.interpretation: Indicates average age of assets. Ratio near 100% suggests fully depreciated assets.

problem_1.question:
A client purchased equipment on July 1 for $120,000. The equipment has a useful life of 10 years and a $20,000 salvage value. The client uses straight-line depreciation. What is the correct depreciation expense for the year ended December 31?

A) $5,000
B) $6,000
C) $10,000
D) $12,000
problem_1.explanation:
Depreciation calculation:
Depreciable cost = $120,000 - $20,000 = $100,000
Annual depreciation = $100,000 ÷ 10 years = $10,000 per year
Partial year (July 1 to Dec 31 = 6 months) = $10,000 × 6/12 = $5,000

B ($6,000) incorrectly doesn't reduce for salvage value: $120,000 ÷ 10 × 6/12 = $6,000 (wrong)
C ($10,000) incorrectly doesn't prorate for partial year
D ($12,000) incorrectly doesn't reduce for salvage value AND doesn't prorate
problem_1.exam_tip: Straight-line depreciation: (Cost - Salvage) ÷ Useful Life × Partial Year Fraction. Always reduce for salvage value and prorate for partial year.

problem_2.question:
An auditor is testing fixed asset additions. Which of the following procedures provides the BEST evidence for the existence of a new machine recorded in fixed assets?

A) Recalculating depreciation expense for the new machine

B) Vouching the recorded cost to the vendor invoice

C) Physically inspecting the machine  

D) Verifying the machine is included in the fixed asset register
problem_2.explanation:
PHYSICAL INSPECTION provides the BEST evidence for EXISTENCE. By physically observing and inspecting the machine, the auditor obtains direct evidence that the asset exists.

A is wrong - recalculating depreciation tests valuation, not existence.
B is wrong - vouching to invoice provides evidence for occurrence and valuation, but invoice alone doesn't prove asset exists (could have been returned, never delivered, etc.).
D is wrong - verifying inclusion in register is circular - just confirms what was recorded, doesn't verify it exists.
problem_2.exam_tip: Physical inspection = EXISTENCE. Vouching to invoices = OCCURRENCE and VALUATION.

problem_3.question:
A client's fixed asset register shows equipment with an original cost of $50,000 and accumulated depreciation of $30,000. The equipment was sold during the year for $25,000. What is the gain or loss on disposal?

A) $5,000 gain
B) $5,000 loss
C) $25,000 gain
D) No gain or loss
problem_3.explanation:
Disposal gain/loss calculation:
Net Book Value = Cost - Accumulated Depreciation = $50,000 - $30,000 = $20,000
Gain/Loss = Proceeds - NBV = $25,000 - $20,000 = $5,000 GAIN

Sold for $25,000, which is $5,000 MORE than NBV of $20,000, so $5,000 gain.

B ($5,000 loss) incorrectly inverts the calculation.
C ($25,000 gain) incorrectly compares proceeds to accumulated depreciation instead of NBV.
D is wrong - there is a gain.
problem_3.exam_tip: Disposal: Gain/Loss = Proceeds - Net Book Value. NBV = Cost - Accumulated Depreciation.

problem_4.question:
An auditor is testing for possible unrecorded fixed asset additions. Which of the following procedures would be MOST effective?

A) Vouching recorded additions to vendor invoices

B) Scanning repairs and maintenance expense for large or unusual items that may be capital in nature

C) Recalculating depreciation expense

D) Confirming additions with vendors
problem_4.explanation:
To find UNRECORDED additions (completeness assertion), the auditor should scan EXPENSE ACCOUNTS (particularly repairs and maintenance) for large items that should have been CAPITALIZED. Items incorrectly expensed represent unrecorded additions to fixed assets.

A is wrong - vouching recorded additions tests existence/occurrence of what's recorded, not completeness (unrecorded).
C is wrong - recalculating depreciation tests valuation of recorded assets, not unrecorded assets.
D is wrong - confirming recorded additions doesn't identify unrecorded items.
problem_4.exam_tip: Testing for UNRECORDED additions (completeness/understatement): scan expense accounts for items that should be capitalized.

problem_5.question:
Under ASC 360, when is an impairment test required for long-lived assets?

A) Annually, at year-end

B) Only when the asset is fully depreciated

C) When indicators of impairment are present

D) Every three years
problem_5.explanation:
Impairment testing for long-lived assets (PP&E) is required when INDICATORS OF IMPAIRMENT are present (not routinely). Indicators include: significant decrease in market value, physical damage, asset idle, adverse business changes, or negative cash flows.

Once indicators identified, perform recoverability test (undiscounted cash flows vs carrying amount). If not recoverable, measure impairment loss (carrying amount - fair value).

A is wrong - annual testing is for goodwill, NOT PP&E.
B is wrong - fully depreciated doesn't trigger impairment test.
D is wrong - not based on time period.
problem_5.exam_tip: PP&E impairment: Test when INDICATORS present (not annual). Step 1: Undiscounted CF vs carrying amount (recoverability). Step 2: Carrying amount - Fair value = impairment loss.

tip_1_test_additions.existence_valuation: Vouch additions to vendor invoices (occurrence, valuation)
tip_1_test_additions.capitalization_decision: Evaluate whether should be capitalized vs expensed
tip_1_test_additions.exam_question: Best evidence for existence of addition? Physical inspection.

tip_2_test_disposals.verify_removed: Verify both cost AND accumulated depreciation removed from books
tip_2_test_disposals.depreciate_through_disposal: Must depreciate through disposal date (partial year if mid-year)

tip_3_depreciation_testing.recalculate: Recalculate depreciation for sample of assets
tip_3_depreciation_testing.verify_useful_lives: Evaluate reasonableness of useful lives (too long = understates expense)
tip_3_depreciation_testing.partial_year: Prorate for assets acquired or disposed during year

tip_4_capitalization_vs_expense.capitalize: New assets, betterments (extend life/increase capacity), major component replacements
tip_4_capitalization_vs_expense.expense: Ordinary repairs and maintenance, small items below threshold
tip_4_capitalization_vs_expense.fraud_risk: Capitalizing ordinary repairs overstates assets and income (common fraud)
tip_4_capitalization_vs_expense.test_both_directions: Vouch additions (should be capital?) AND scan expenses (should be capital?)

tip_5_impairment_testing.step_1_recoverability: UNDISCOUNTED cash flows vs Carrying Amount (if CF < CA, proceed to step 2)
tip_5_impairment_testing.step_2_measurement: Impairment Loss = Carrying Amount - FAIR VALUE
tip_5_impairment_testing.cannot_reverse: Once recognized, cannot reverse impairment loss
tip_5_impairment_testing.exam_trick: Step 1 uses UNDISCOUNTED CF. Step 2 uses FAIR VALUE (may be discounted).

tip_6_physical_inspection.when_performed: Significant additions, fraud risk, portable assets, first-year audit (not always required)
tip_6_physical_inspection.two_directions: Register to floor (existence) AND floor to register (completeness)
tip_6_physical_inspection.what_it_tests: Existence and condition - does NOT test valuation or ownership

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Calculate depreciation for partial year acquisition
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: (Cost - Salvage) ÷ Useful Life × Months Owned / 12. Don't forget partial year!
NBV = Cost - Accum Depr. Gain/Loss = Proceeds - NBV. Must depreciate through disposal date first.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: What procedure provides best evidence for existence of addition?
How to test for unrecorded additions?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Scan repairs/maintenance expense for items that should be capitalized
When INDICATORS present (not annual). Use undiscounted CF for recoverability, fair value for measurement.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Should expenditure be capitalized or expensed?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Capitalize if: provides future benefit, meets threshold, extends life/increases capacity. Expense if: ordinary repairs, below threshold.

memorization_aids.impairment_steps: Step 1: UNdiscounted CF (recoverability). Step 2: Fair Value (measurement)

key_concepts: Test additions: vouch to invoices (occurrence, valuation), physically inspect (existence), evaluate capitalization decision
Test disposals: verify both cost and accumulated depreciation removed, recalculate gain/loss (Proceeds - NBV)
Depreciation: recalculate for sample, verify useful lives reasonable, partial year for mid-year additions/disposals
Physical inspection tests existence and condition (not valuation or ownership)
Capitalize: new assets, betterments extending life/capacity. Expense: ordinary repairs, items below threshold
Fraud risk: capitalizing ordinary repairs overstates assets and income
Test for unrecorded additions: scan repairs expense for capital items
Impairment: test when indicators present. Step 1: undiscounted CF vs carrying amount. Step 2: carrying amount - fair value
Lease classification: if any of 5 criteria met = finance lease (capitalize). Otherwise operating lease.
critical_for_exam: Depreciation calculation: (Cost - Salvage) ÷ Useful Life × Partial Year
Gain/loss on disposal: Proceeds - NBV (where NBV = Cost - Accumulated Depreciation)
Physical inspection = best evidence for existence
Test for unrecorded additions by scanning expense accounts
Impairment: Step 1 undiscounted CF, Step 2 fair value
Capitalize betterments that extend life/capacity. Expense ordinary repairs.
Capitalizing repairs = common fraud (overstates assets and income)
common_mistakes: Forgetting to subtract salvage value in straight-line depreciation calculation
Not prorating depreciation for partial year acquisitions/disposals
Thinking vouching to invoice is best evidence for existence (NO - physical inspection is best)
Confusing PP&E impairment (indicators-based) with goodwill impairment (annual)
Using discounted cash flows in Step 1 of impairment (NO - use undiscounted for recoverability test)
Thinking land is depreciated (NO - land has indefinite life, never depreciate)
Not recognizing that capitalizing ordinary repairs is a fraud scheme
Forgetting to remove accumulated depreciation when asset disposed (not just cost)
